points.text: Novelty weak: entropy reward hacking already known; no remedy offered
Experiments only on small models; need more diverse base models
No formal results in main paper for SimPO-MaxEnt connection; conditions unclear
Equivalence non-rigorous: length-normalized alpha prevents partition function cancellation
Online failure claims rest on Pythia-1B/2.8B; larger models untested
Only TL;DR summarization; more complex alignment tasks untested
Response-dependent alpha breaks MaxEnt connection; length normalization unanalyzed
Margin gamma not related to maximum-entropy RL
Only small Pythia models; generalization to Qwen/LLaMA unclear
Limited contribution; implications for preference algorithm design unclear
Online failure of MaxEnt RL lacks theoretical explanation
Theory largely a trivial relabelling of reward as log-likelihood
Partition function cancellation fails with response-dependent alpha; Eq.15 to 16 not derived
Margin gamma added by analogy, not derived
Inherited DPO guarantees not checked for length-normalized case
MaxEnt observation already made by Liu et al.; incremental theory
Online experiment tests a different objective than offline SimPO; asymmetry confounded
No SimPO-style online or unregularized RL baseline; limitation conclusion unsupported
KL and MaxEnt runs use different learning rates and coefficients; no matched sweep
Admitted KL beta sensitivity weakens KL-stable narrative
No seeds, error bars or confidence intervals; single runs
Several results described in text only without data
Causal claim that entropy exacerbates reward hacking unsupported
Missing zero-coefficient / plain RL control at same learning rates
Section 4.3 mechanism rests on one DPO diagnostic
No SimPO experiment, gamma ablation or other offline comparison
Chi-squared result not reproducible and undetailed
Only Pythia 1B/2.8B on TL;DR with small RM and one judge; generality overstated
No human evaluation
Reproducibility claimed without code or configs
Presentation: inconsistent hedging, figure order, typos
